🇲🇽🇪🇸 SPAIN'S KING CAME TO MEXICO — AND THE TERMS HAD CHANGED

King Felipe VI met President Sheinbaum at Palacio Nacional — the first meeting between a Spanish monarch and a Mexican head of state since AMLO froze ties over Madrid's refusal to apologize for the conquest. The thaw came only after Felipe VI publicly acknowledged there was "much abuse" during the conquest. Mexico never dropped the demand; Spain moved toward it.

🌽🇲🇽 MEXICO PROJECTED TO STAY THE WORLD'S #1 CORN IMPORTER THROUGH 2035

A new OECD–FAO outlook projects Mexico will absorb 10% of all global corn imports by 2035 — the single largest share on the planet, ahead of the EU (9%), Vietnam (8%), Japan (7%) and China (3%). The overwhelming majority comes from the United States. This is exactly why the Fourth Transformation's push for food sovereignty — and AMLO's fight to keep US GM corn out of the tortilla — was never just symbolism.

🚨🇲🇽 TELECOM GIANTS LEGALLY REQUIRED TO DESTROY CUSTOMERS' BIOMETRIC DATA

As Mexico's mobile-line registry deadline hits June 30, operators Telcel, AT&T, Movistar and Altán Redes are legally required to destroy the biometric data they collected from customers linking their lines to the CURP — it was for identity verification only, not a database to keep. The catch, per the Mexican Internet Association: the companies "neither inform nor provide evidence" that they aren't holding on to it. Your biometrics aren't a corporate asset, and Mexicans are right to demand proof.

KPBS: Mexico's President Visits Tijuana to Promote Education
June 22, 2026 | 🟢

A US public-radio station covers Sheinbaum opening a tech high school and launching the universal Rita Cetina scholarship at the border — quoted directly, no cartel hook forced in.

"Education is a right, not a privilege." Proof US outlets can cover Mexico's social programs straight when they choose to.

• Sheinbaum: "Education is a right, not a privilege"
• New universal scholarship named for 19th-c. feminist literacy activist Rita Cetina Gutiérrez

NTD / SENATE DRUG CAUCUS: Beyond Our Shores — The Global Reach of Mexican Drug Cartels
June 24, 2026 | 🔴

A Senate caucus convenes a hearing titled "Beyond Our Shores" to map Mexican cartels as a planetary terror threat — Brookings analysts and an ex-DEA agent testify, not one Mexican official in the room.

Unmentioned: the US guns flowing south, and Mexico's own data showing homicides at an 11-year low and 40,000 arrests over the past year.

• Cornyn: cartels fetch "double the price for cocaine in Europe"
• The case rests on 2025's terror designations of Sinaloa and CJNG

AL JAZEERA: If USMCA Is Not Renewed, Analysts Expect Uncertainty for Businesses
June 28, 2026 | 🟡

With the July 1 USMCA review looming, Trump shrugs: "I would rather not have the agreement, but I may sign it." The economic future of three countries hangs on a maybe.

More than 80% of Mexican exports go north — yet the piece treats Mexico as a spectator to its own trade deal, quoting Trump and US analysts while Sheinbaum's government goes unmentioned.

• Trump: "I don't know that I'm going to renew it"
• Trump: "I would rather not have the agreement, but I may sign it"

🇲🇽🏭 T-MEC REVIEW OPENS JULY 1 — AND MEXICO HOLDS A STRONG HAND

The formal T-MEC review kicks off July 1 with a trilateral meeting between Mexico's Marcelo Ebrard, US trade rep Jamieson Greer and Canada's Dominic LeBlanc. Sheinbaum is clear: it's "a review, not a renegotiation." Mexico's leverage is structural — North America's dependence on Asian semiconductors tops 85%, and Mexico, supplying just 3-4% of US chip demand today, stands to multiply that sixfold as Washington scrambles to pull supply chains out of Asia.

🚨🇲🇽 "COLLABORATION IS ONE THING, INTERFERENCE IS ANOTHER" — MEXICO DRAWS THE LINE

As Washington escalates — CIA agents operating in Chihuahua without notifying the federal government, ratings agencies arbitrarily downgrading the country — Sheinbaum's answer is blunt: "Una cosa es colaboración y otra injerencia." And she negotiates from strength: homicides down 49% since 2024, unemployment at 2.5%, and the minimum wage up 154% since 2018.

🔥🇲🇽 SALINAS PLIEGO'S BETTING HOUSES CAUGHT IN MONEY-LAUNDERING DRAGNET

Mexico's Financial Intelligence Unit (UIF), working with the US OFAC, has 39 corporate groups that control the country's casinos under investigation for laundering narco money — and has already suspended the online betting houses Ganador Azteca and Operadora Ganador TV Azteca, both owned by Ricardo Salinas Pliego's Grupo Salinas, plus casinos Centenario, Diamante, Midas and Palermo. The operations spanned Jalisco, Nuevo León, Sonora, Sinaloa and five other states.

🚨🇲🇽 MEXICO BETS ON PEACE THROUGH JUSTICE — NOT TANKS — IN MICHOACÁN

While Washington pushes a militarized "war on cartels," Sheinbaum's government is pouring more than 57 billion pesos into Michoacán under a plan whose stated mission is to turn the state into "a humanist and economic power" — including 37.45 billion pesos in 2026 for scholarships and Bienestar programs reaching 1.5 million people. Security built on education, health, housing and dignified work, not occupation.
